front.title: A RATS Profile for Attestation of AI Inference Model Admission and Runtime Binding

abstract.t:
AI inference environments dynamically load, transform, configure, and execute model artifacts across heterogeneous software and hardware trust domains. Independent measurements of model artifacts and inference runtimes do not establish that a particular model representation was admitted into a particular runtime instance or maintained within the execution environment.
This document specifies a Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) profile for cryptographically protected evidence of AI inference model admission and runtime binding.
The profile defines an information model and processing requirements for identifying source model artifacts, recording transformation provenance, measuring admitted model representations, identifying inference-runtime instances, and establishing a protected association between admitted representations and execution environments.
The profile builds on the RATS architecture, the Entity Attestation Token (EAT), and the EAT measured-component information model. It defines requirements for model identity, transformation continuity, admission events, runtime identity, evidence protection, freshness, and verifier appraisal.
The resulting evidence enables a Verifier to evaluate whether an identified model representation was admitted into an identified inference-runtime instance within the declared attestation boundary.
